interactions.summary: Jiang cites media elites and Trump himself as evidence that a pro-rapprochement campaign is already underway and predicts a near-term grand bargain between the United States and China brokered by billionaire interests.
Sneako asks whether stable coins and crypto-backed legislation are really part of a strategy to manage America's massive debt burden.
Jiang says the GENIUS and CLARITY acts would force digital-currency issuers to hold U.S. Treasuries, which he treats as a mechanism for financial repression and compulsory treasury demand.
Sneako asks for clarification on whether a Treasury is basically an IOU rather than actual money.

Jiang explains Treasuries as government bonds issued into a monetary system run by private-bank power through the Federal Reserve, then says stable coins would retailize access to those bonds for individuals worldwide.

claims.claim: Jiang says establishment voices are already normalizing a U.S.-China rapprochement by portraying China as weak, manageable, and worth doing business with rather than fighting.
claims.temporal_scope: Current media and geopolitical diagnosis on 2026-05-18.

claims.claim: He predicts that a massive U.S.-China grand bargain will emerge within the next few months and says billionaire interests want access to Chinese consumers and capital through treasury-linked stable coins.

Jiang says the GENIUS Act and CLARITY Act are designed to require stable-coin issuers such as Tether or Circle to hold U.S. Treasuries in reserve, thereby forcing treasury demand regardless of interest rates.
He describes financial repression as a strategy of pushing interest rates toward zero while simultaneously forcing investors into Treasuries so the state can keep servicing its debt burden.

Jiang says the Federal Reserve is not truly a government body but a committee of private-bank interests that creates money, while the government finances spending by issuing Treasury bonds into that system.
He argues that stable coins turn Treasury ownership from an institutional practice into a retail product that any individual in the world could buy.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang treats the coming U.S.-China accommodation as a billionaire-brokered financial opening rather than a diplomatic reconciliation.
signature_moments.source_phrase: you're going to see this massive grand bargain
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's forward-looking center of gravity and ties the China story directly to debt, treasury demand, and stable-coin infrastructure.

signature_moments.moment: Legislation is portrayed not as crypto modernization but as an engineered pipeline into U.S. debt.
signature_moments.source_phrase: you have to have us treasuries in reserve
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It compresses Jiang's whole interpretation of stable-coin policy into one coercive mechanism.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang strips the mystique from the Federal Reserve by calling it neither federal, nor reserve, nor bank.
signature_moments.source_phrase: it's not government ... it's not a reserve and it's not a bank
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is his most memorable reframing of the U.S. monetary system as private-bank rule masked by public language.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's label for lowering interest rates toward zero while coercing demand for Treasury debt so the state can keep carrying a huge debt load.
Digital-currency instruments that Jiang says will be required to hold U.S. Treasuries and will turn Treasury ownership into a global retail channel.
Long-term U.S. government bonds that finance state spending and, in Jiang's telling, sit at the center of the stable-coin expansion strategy.

chronology_notes.note: Jiang moves from immediate post-visit media messaging in the present to a prediction about what will happen over the next few months if the rapprochement project succeeds.

uncertainty_notes.note: Some names and details in Jiang's list of commentators are transcript-grounded but likely partly garbled by ASR, so the packet preserves the thrust of the media chorus without overcommitting to exact wording.
The debt figure and the exact legislative mechanisms are presented as claims inside the interview and are not independently verified within this packet.
